# duploai_azure_managed_redis (Resource)

Manages an Azure Managed Redis (Redis Enterprise) instance, provisioned within an environment and resource group.

Azure models this as two ARM resources and the platform creates both: a `Microsoft.Cache/redisEnterprise` cluster (SKU, TLS, high availability, public network access) and a single `Microsoft.Cache/redisEnterprise/databases` child named `default` (clustering policy, eviction policy, modules, persistence, geo-replication, access-key auth). The attributes below are flattened across both. The database child is created only after the cluster finishes provisioning, so `database_id` and the access-key operations are unavailable for a period after the resource first reports Complete — set `wait_for_database` if you need to depend on them.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# A minimal instance: the smallest fixed-size SKU, TLS-only, no public endpoint.
resource "duploai_azure_managed_redis" "cache" {
  workspace_id      = "<workspace-id>"
  environment_id    = "<environment-id>"
  resource_group_id = "<resource-group-id>"

  name     = "app-cache"
  sku_name = "Balanced_B1"

  tags = {
    app = "payments"
  }
}

# A larger instance with persistence. Cache size comes from the SKU name — every
# supported family is fixed-size, so there is no capacity/shard setting, and zone
# redundancy is automatic (Azure Managed Redis rejects explicit zones).
#
# The legacy Enterprise_* / EnterpriseFlash_* SKUs are NOT supported: those are Azure
# Cache for Redis Enterprise, which Azure has retired, and a create is rejected with
# "Creation of new Azure Cache for Redis Enterprise resources is no longer supported".
resource "duploai_azure_managed_redis" "bigger" {
  workspace_id      = "<workspace-id>"
  environment_id    = "<environment-id>"
  resource_group_id = "<resource-group-id>"

  name     = "shared-cache"
  sku_name = "MemoryOptimized_M10"

  eviction_policy = "AllKeysLRU"

  persistence = {
    rdb_enabled   = true
    rdb_frequency = "SixHours"
  }
}

# Modules can only be enabled when the database is first created, so adding or
# removing one later forces replacement. RediSearch additionally requires
# EnterpriseCluster clustering. Everything else on the instance (tags, eviction
# policy, persistence) still updates in place.
resource "duploai_azure_managed_redis" "search" {
  workspace_id      = "<workspace-id>"
  environment_id    = "<environment-id>"
  resource_group_id = "<resource-group-id>"

  name              = "search-cache"
  sku_name          = "Balanced_B10"
  clustering_policy = "EnterpriseCluster"

  modules = [
    { name = "RediSearch" },
    { name = "RedisBloom", args = "ERROR_RATE 0.01 INITIAL_SIZE 400" },
  ]
}

# Access keys are disabled by default, since Azure now steers new caches towards
# Microsoft Entra ID authentication. Enable them only if a client cannot use Entra —
# while disabled, the platform's key read/regenerate operations return an error
# because Azure rejects ListKeys.
#
# The setting can be changed in place. Note the platform's own console cannot: its
# save payload resends the current value rather than the newly selected one, so the
# toggle appears to revert. Terraform sends the value you configure.
#
# wait_for_database makes the apply block until the `default` database child exists.
# The cluster reports Complete first and the database is created afterwards, so
# without this `database_id` can still be empty when dependent resources run.
resource "duploai_azure_managed_redis" "with_keys" {
  workspace_id      = "<workspace-id>"
  environment_id    = "<environment-id>"
  resource_group_id = "<resource-group-id>"

  name     = "legacy-client-cache"
  sku_name = "Balanced_B1"

  access_keys_authentication_enabled = true
  wait_for_database                  = true
}

# Active geo-replication. Azure only accepts these settings when the database is
# created, so a group is built by creating both members with it already configured:
# the first with a nickname and an empty link list, the second referencing the
# first's database_id. wait_for_database on the first is required — its database_id
# is empty until the database child finishes provisioning. Azure then links both
# ends itself, so the first member reports the second without Terraform sending it.
#
# WARNING: a geo-replicated instance cannot be UPDATED afterwards at all — not even
# its tags. Every update is rejected with "Cannot change spec.geoReplication after
# creation", because the platform compares the configured peer list against Azure's
# member list (which includes the database itself) and the two can never match.
# Replace the instance to change anything. Geo-replication also requires high
# availability, rejects the Balanced_B0/B1 and FlashOptimized_* SKUs, cannot be
# combined with persistence, and tolerates only the RediSearch and RedisJSON modules.
resource "duploai_azure_managed_redis" "geo_primary" {
  workspace_id      = "<workspace-id>"
  environment_id    = "<environment-id>"
  resource_group_id = "<resource-group-id>"

  name              = "cache-east"
  sku_name          = "Balanced_B3"
  high_availability = true

  geo_replication = {
    group_nickname          = "prod-cache-group"
    linked_database_arm_ids = []
  }

  wait_for_database = true
}

resource "duploai_azure_managed_redis" "geo_secondary" {
  workspace_id      = "<workspace-id>"
  environment_id    = "<environment-id>"
  resource_group_id = "<resource-group-id>"

  name              = "cache-west"
  sku_name          = "Balanced_B3"
  high_availability = true

  geo_replication = {
    group_nickname          = "prod-cache-group"
    linked_database_arm_ids = [duploai_azure_managed_redis.geo_primary.database_id]
  }

  wait_for_database = true
}

output "endpoint" {
  value = "${duploai_azure_managed_redis.cache.host_name}:${duploai_azure_managed_redis.cache.port}"
}

output "database_id" {
  value = duploai_azure_managed_redis.with_keys.database_id
}
```

## Schema

### Required

- `environment_id` (String) ID of the environment in which the Redis instance is provisioned.
- `name` (String) Redis instance name. 1-60 characters, alphanumeric and hyphens, first and last character alphanumeric, no consecutive hyphens, and globally unique across Azure. Immutable after creation.
- `resource_group_id` (String) ID of the resource group in which the Redis instance is provisioned.
- `workspace_id` (String) ID of the workspace that owns this Redis instance.

### Optional

- `access_keys_authentication_enabled` (Boolean) Allow classic access-key authentication. Defaults to disabled, matching Azure's guidance to use Microsoft Entra ID for new caches. While disabled, the platform's access-key read and regenerate operations return an error, because Azure rejects ListKeys outright. Can be changed in place — verified live 2026-08-04. The platform's own console cannot change it: its save payload resends the current value rather than the newly selected one, so the toggle appears to revert.
- `clustering_policy` (String) Redis clustering policy. Treated as immutable here: Azure only allows it to change while the current value is `NoCluster`, so a change forces replacement rather than risking an update the API rejects. `EnterpriseCluster` is required by the RediSearch module. `NoCluster` additionally only applies to SKUs of 25 GB or less and is not supported at all by the `FlashOptimized_*` family; the API rejects both cases.
- `eviction_policy` (String) Key eviction policy applied when the cache is full.
- `failure_retries` (Number) Number of extra polls to tolerate a transient failure status during provisioning before treating it as terminal. Overrides the resource's default; leave unset to use it.
- `geo_replication` (Attributes) Active geo-replication group membership. Immutable: any change here REPLACES the instance. Azure only accepts geo-replication settings when the database is created, so the platform rejects an edit outright and Azure answers the underlying request with an opaque 501.

Build a group by creating both members with it already configured: give the first a `group_nickname` and an empty `linked_database_arm_ids`, then create the second with the same nickname and the first's `database_id` in its link list. Azure then links both ends itself — the first database reports the second as a member without Terraform ever sending it, so `geo_replication_linked_database_ids` on the first member will show a value its own configuration does not, and a refresh reports that as an out-of-band change. Leaving `linked_database_arm_ids` empty with no nickname creates an ordinary standalone database. Verified live 2026-08-04.

Setting either field here counts as enabling geo-replication, which brings four constraints: it requires `high_availability = true`; it is rejected on the `Balanced_B0`, `Balanced_B1` and every `FlashOptimized_*` SKU; it cannot be combined with `persistence`; and the only modules it tolerates are `RediSearch` and `RedisJSON`.

WARNING: while geo-replication is enabled the instance cannot be UPDATED AT ALL — not even its tags. The platform validates geo-replication immutability by comparing the requested `linked_database_arm_ids` against Azure's reported member list within the same request body, and those two can never match: the configured list holds the peers, while Azure's holds every member including the database itself. Every update is therefore rejected with "Cannot change spec.geoReplication after creation", whatever it actually changed. This affects the platform's own console equally. Treat a geo-replicated instance as immutable and replace it to change anything. Verified live 2026-08-04. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--geo_replication))
- `high_availability` (Boolean) Replicate the data set within the cluster. Enabled by default, which is also what `persistence` and `geo_replication` require — setting this to `false` makes either of them fail. Disabling it lowers the availability SLA and increases the risk of data loss.
- `minimum_tls_version` (String) Minimum TLS version the cluster accepts. `Tls1_2` is the only accepted value — TLS 1.0 and 1.1 are obsolete on Azure Managed Redis and the API rejects them. The attribute exists so the value is explicit in configuration and state, and so a future version can be added without a breaking change.
- `modules` (Attributes List) Redis modules to enable, e.g. RediSearch, RedisBloom, RedisJSON, RedisTimeSeries. Immutable after creation — Azure only accepts modules when the database is first created, so a change forces replacement. RediSearch additionally requires `clustering_policy = "EnterpriseCluster"`. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--modules))
- `non_tls_access_enabled` (Boolean) Also accept plaintext Redis connections alongside TLS. Defaults to TLS-only.
- `persistence` (Attributes) Data persistence (backup) settings. At most one of `rdb_enabled` / `aof_enabled` may be true — Azure rejects both — and whichever is enabled requires its matching frequency. Enabling either requires `high_availability = true`, and cannot be combined with `geo_replication`. That conflict is enforced at plan time against the presence of the two blocks, which is slightly stricter than the API: it also rejects a persistence block whose flags are all `false` alongside `geo_replication`, where the API would accept it. Omit the block entirely in that case — an all-`false` persistence block does nothing. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--persistence))
- `provisioner_type` (String) Provisioner type. Assigned by the platform when unset — existing instances report `Cli`.
- `provisioner_version` (String) Optional provisioner version. Left unset the API omits it, so this reads back empty rather than as an empty string.
- `public_network_access_enabled` (Boolean) Expose the cluster's public endpoint. Defaults to disabled per platform policy, in which case the cluster is reachable only through a Private Endpoint.
- `sku_name` (String) Azure Managed Redis SKU. Cache size is fixed by the SKU name across all four supported families (Balanced, MemoryOptimized, ComputeOptimized, FlashOptimized). Immutable after creation.

The legacy `Enterprise_*` and `EnterpriseFlash_*` families are deliberately not offered: those are Azure Cache for Redis Enterprise SKUs, which Azure has retired — a create returns "Creation of new Azure Cache for Redis Enterprise resources is no longer supported". They are therefore unusable here, including for adopting an existing legacy instance.
- `tags` (Map of String) Tags applied to the Redis instance. The platform adds its own managed `duplocloud-ai-*` tags server-side; those are filtered out of state so only your tags are managed by Terraform.
- `timeouts` (Block, Optional) (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--timeouts))
- `wait_for_database` (Boolean) When true, wait during create and update until the backend reports a value at result.databaseId (e.g. a provisioned load balancer address), or the operation times out. Defaults to false.

### Read-Only

- `azure_resource_group_name` (String) Azure resource group the cluster is created in, derived from the linked resource group.
- `cluster_id` (String) Full Azure resource ID (ARM ID) of the Redis Enterprise cluster.
- `created_at` (String) Timestamp when the Redis instance was created (RFC 3339).
- `database_id` (String) Full Azure resource ID (ARM ID) of the `default` database. Empty until the database child finishes provisioning, which happens after the cluster — set `wait_for_database` to block until it is populated.
- `geo_replication_group_nickname` (String) Geo-replication group nickname reported by Azure, if the database belongs to a group.
- `geo_replication_linked_database_ids` (List of String) ARM resource IDs of the other databases linked in the same geo-replication group, as reported by Azure.
- `host_name` (String) Redis endpoint hostname, e.g. myredis.eastus.redisenterprise.cache.azure.net.
- `id` (String) Composite resource identifier (workspace_id/id).
- `port` (Number) TCP port of the database endpoint.
- `provisioning_state` (String) Azure provisioning state of the cluster, e.g. Succeeded or Creating.
- `redis_id` (String) ID of this Redis instance, for reference by dependent resources.
- `reported_modules` (Attributes List) Modules as Azure reports them, mirroring `modules`. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--reported_modules))
- `scope_ids` (List of String) Scope IDs linking this Redis instance to a cloud provider account, inherited from the resource group.
- `status` (String) Current provisioning status of the Redis instance.
- `unique_cloud_resource_id` (String) Full Azure resource ID (ARM ID) of the cluster, as the platform records it on the resource itself. `cluster_id` exposes the same ARM ID read from the live Azure result.
- `updated_at` (String) Timestamp when the Redis instance was last updated (RFC 3339).
- `version` (Number) Version counter, incremented on each update.

<a id="nestedatt--geo_replication"></a>
### Nested Schema for `geo_replication`

Optional:

- `group_nickname` (String) Shared name identifying the geo-replication group. Required when `linked_database_arm_ids` is non-empty.
- `linked_database_arm_ids` (List of String) Full ARM resource IDs of the other databases already in the group.


<a id="nestedatt--modules"></a>
### Nested Schema for `modules`

Required:

- `name` (String) Module name, e.g. `RediSearch`, `RedisBloom`, `RedisJSON`, `RedisTimeSeries`. `RediSearch` requires `clustering_policy` = EnterpriseCluster and `eviction_policy` = NoEviction; with `geo_replication` enabled, only `RediSearch` and `RedisJSON` are accepted at all.

Optional:

- `args` (String) Optional module configuration string, e.g. `ERROR_RATE 0.01 INITIAL_SIZE 400`.


<a id="nestedatt--persistence"></a>
### Nested Schema for `persistence`

Optional:

- `aof_enabled` (Boolean) Enable append-only-file persistence.
- `aof_frequency` (String) Append-only-file write frequency. Required when `aof_enabled` is true.
- `rdb_enabled` (Boolean) Enable RDB snapshot persistence.
- `rdb_frequency` (String) Snapshot interval. Required when `rdb_enabled` is true.


<a id="nestedblock--timeouts"></a>
### Nested Schema for `timeouts`

Optional:

- `create` (String) A string that can be [parsed as a duration](https://pkg.go.dev/time#ParseDuration) consisting of numbers and unit suffixes, such as "30s" or "2h45m". Valid time units are "s" (seconds), "m" (minutes), "h" (hours).
- `delete` (String) A string that can be [parsed as a duration](https://pkg.go.dev/time#ParseDuration) consisting of numbers and unit suffixes, such as "30s" or "2h45m". Valid time units are "s" (seconds), "m" (minutes), "h" (hours). Setting a timeout for a Delete operation is only applicable if changes are saved into state before the destroy operation occurs.
- `update` (String) A string that can be [parsed as a duration](https://pkg.go.dev/time#ParseDuration) consisting of numbers and unit suffixes, such as "30s" or "2h45m". Valid time units are "s" (seconds), "m" (minutes), "h" (hours).


<a id="nestedatt--reported_modules"></a>
### Nested Schema for `reported_modules`

Read-Only:

- `args` (String) Module configuration string, empty when none.
- `name` (String) Module name.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Import an existing Azure Managed Redis instance.
#  - WORKSPACE_ID is the ID of the workspace (e.g. 69b2aa30675718845bfe87a0)
#  - REDIS_ID is the ID of the Redis instance (e.g. 6a2258e94703bc957a1b824e)
terraform import duploai_azure_managed_redis.cache WORKSPACE_ID/REDIS_ID
# Example:
# terraform import duploai_azure_managed_redis.cache 69b2aa30675718845bfe87a0/6a2258e94703bc957a1b824e
#
# wait_for_database is a Terraform-only control attribute — it drives how long an
# apply waits and is not stored by the API, so it lands false after an import. Set it
# in config if you want it; that produces no API call.
```
